locator: CCC 31-34, not in the sense of proofs in the natural sciences, but rather in the sense of converging and convincing arguments
interpretation: CCC 31: 'These are also called proofs for the existence of God, not in the sense of proofs in the natural sciences, but rather in the sense of "converging and convincing arguments", which allow us to attain certainty about the truth'; CCC 32 cites Rom 1:19-20 on the Gentiles; CCC 34: man can come to know a reality 'that everyone calls God'. The contrast with the natural sciences is kept: a fideist may read it as a mark of a distinct standard.
attribution: The passage states that the ways of coming to know God are called proofs, not in the natural sciences' sense but as converging and convincing arguments that allow certainty, starting from the world and the human person, by which man can know a first cause and final end that everyone calls God, which is the premise.
